title: Mathematics AI HL — Set B Paper 3

questions.stem:
A laboratory heating device receives two current components with the same period of $12$ seconds. Their combined current, in amperes, is modelled by

$$I(t)=4\cos(\omega t)+3\cos(\omega t-\phi),\qquad \omega=\frac{\pi}{6},\qquad 0\le\phi\le\pi.$$

The adjustable phase is $\phi$. Write the combined current as $I(t)=A\cos(\omega t-\delta)$ with $A>0$. A phasor diagram is shown for one phase choice.

When current is supplied to the heater, its useful instantaneous heating power is $10I(t)^2$ watts. A safety controller diverts the current away from the heater whenever $|I(t)|>4$ A. While diverted, the useful power is zero; the input current model itself is unchanged. Let $q$ be the fraction of a complete period for which the heater is off.

For any periodic power function $p(t)$ with period $12$ s, its mean power is

$$\overline P=\frac1{12}\int_0^{12}p(t)\,\mathrm dt.$$

You may use $\cos^2u=(1+\cos2u)/2$. All angles are in radians.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: For $\phi=1.2$, use the complex number $Z=4+3e^{-i\phi}$ to find $A$ and $\delta$, giving $0\le\delta<\pi$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For variable $\phi$, show that $A^2=25+24\cos\phi$. Hence state the possible range of $A$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If the safety controller were removed, show that the mean heating power over a complete period would be $5A^2$ watts.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For $A>4$, obtain $q$ in terms of $A$. Also state $q$ when $1\le A\le4$.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The permitted fraction of time off is at most $1/4$. Find the resulting interval of permissible phases $\phi$.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: With the controller operating, obtain an expression for the mean useful power $P(A)$ for $1\le A\le4$, and for $4<A\le7$. Show the integration leading to your expression. You may use symmetry over one complete phase cycle.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: Use technology to investigate $P(A)$ under the restriction in part (e). Find the phase that maximizes mean useful power and the resulting maximum. Support your conclusion over the whole permitted domain. Explain why choosing the largest permitted amplitude is not optimal.

questions.answerSummary: At $\phi=1.2$, $A=5.80487606$, $\delta=0.502575580$. $A\in[1,7]$. $q=0$ for $A\le4$, otherwise $q=2\arccos(4/A)/\pi$. Permitted $\phi\in[1.834458682,\pi]$. $P=5A^2$ for $A\le4$; otherwise $P=10A^2[\arcsin(4/A)-(4/A)\sqrt{1-16/A^2}]/\pi$. Global optimum $A=4$, $\phi=\arccos(-3/8)=1.955193101$, $P=80$ W.

steps.text: $\delta=-\arg Z=0.5025755802\ldots\approx0.503$ radians, so the combined cosine is delayed by $\delta$.
$A^2=16+24\cos\phi+9(\cos^2\phi+\sin^2\phi)=25+24\cos\phi$.
As $\phi$ ranges from $0$ to $\pi$, $1\le A\le7$.
Use the average $\frac{10A^2}{12}\int_0^{12}\cos^2(\omega t-\delta)\,\mathrm dt$.
Using the provided identity, the oscillatory cosine term has integral zero over a whole period and the constant term integrates to $6$.
The unrestricted mean power is $5A^2$ W, independent of $\delta$.
For $c=4/A\in(0,1)$, the controller is off when $|\cos u|>c$.
Over a phase interval of length $2\pi$, this has total length $4\arccos c$.
$q=2\arccos(4/A)/\pi$ for $A>4$.
For $1\le A\le4$, the threshold is never exceeded and $q=0$.
$2\arccos(4/A)/\pi\le1/4$ gives $A\le4/\cos(\pi/8)$, including the $A\le4$ cases.
$\arccos((16\sec^2(\pi/8)-25)/24)\le\phi\le\pi$, or $1.834458682\ldots\le\phi\le\pi$.
A full-period average is unaffected by the phase shift; work with $u$ over $0\le u\le2\pi$.
For $A>4$, put $c=4/A$ and use symmetry: $P=\frac{10A^2}{2\pi}\,4\int_{\arccos c}^{\pi/2}\cos^2u\,\mathrm du$.
An antiderivative is $u/2+\sin(2u)/4$.
The integral of $\cos^2u$ over all on-intervals is $2\arcsin c-2c\sqrt{1-c^2}$.
$P(A)=\frac{10A^2}{\pi}\left[\arcsin(4/A)-\frac4A\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{A^2}}\right]$ W for $4<A\le7$.
For $1\le A\le4$, there is no shutdown and $P(A)=5A^2$ W. Both expressions approach $80$ W at $A=4$.
Investigate the piecewise function on the full permitted interval $1\le A\le4\sec(\pi/8)=4.329568801\ldots$.
The maximum is $80$ W at $A=4$.

Support globality with a labelled graph or equivalent numerical/analytic investigation showing increase up to $4$ and decrease from just above $4$ to the upper bound. A single isolated calculator maximum is insufficient.
$\phi=\arccos((16-25)/24)=\arccos(-3/8)=1.955193101\ldots\approx1.96$ radians.
Above $A=4$, the largest instantaneous powers are discarded by shutdown. Increasing amplitude increases lost peak intervals; a larger permitted amplitude therefore produces less useful mean power.

questions.stem:
A maintenance crew must inspect every link of an underground service network. The undirected graph has the eight edges shown; edge weights are traversal times in minutes. Inspecting a link requires traversing the whole edge at least once. Edges may be repeated, and there are no junctions at crossings in the diagram.

The time on link $AD$ is a positive parameter $w$. All other times are fixed. Unless a part states otherwise, the crew starts and finishes at $A$. The aim is to minimize total traversal time, including repeated edges. Denote this minimum closed-route time by $L_c(w)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the odd-degree vertices. Explain why the crew cannot inspect all eight links exactly once on a closed route.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For $w=2$, construct a table of shortest traversal times between the odd-degree vertices. Show any indirect paths used.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For $w=2$, find the minimum closed-route time and give one route attaining it. Justify why a shorter closed route is impossible.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Investigate how the optimal repeated links change as $w$ varies. Obtain an exact piecewise expression for $L_c(w)$ for all $w>0$, justifying the breakpoint and all candidate pairings.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The link $AD$ is removed from the inspection network. Find the new minimum closed-route time. Explain why removing a useful connection can nevertheless shorten an inspection route.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Instead, keep all eight links, but allow the crew to start at $A$ and finish at $D$. Show that the minimum open-route time is $L_o(w)=44+w$ for all $w>0$.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: An open route incurs an additional return cost equivalent to $h>0$ minutes. Derive a complete decision rule in terms of $w$ and $h$ for choosing a closed route or an open route plus return. Include all tie cases. Explain why the maximum possible saving in traversal time from using an open route is only $3$ minutes, however large $w$ becomes.

questions.answerSummary: Odd vertices $A,B,D,E$. At $w=2$ minimum added time is $9$ and $L_c=48$. In general $L_c(w)=44+2w$ for $0<w\le3$, and $47+w$ for $w\ge3$. Removing $AD$ gives $44$. $L_o=44+w$. Open plus return is strictly better iff $h<3$ and $w>h$. Closed is strictly better iff $h>\min(w,3)$; ties are $h=\min(w,3)$.

steps.text: $A,B,D,E$ each have degree $3$; $C,F$ have degree $2$.
A closed Eulerian route requires every degree even. Four odd vertices prevent traversing every edge exactly once on a closed route.
Use shortest paths, including $A\to D\to E$ for $AE$ and $B\to A\to D$ for $BD$.
For the order $(A,B,D,E)$, shortest distances are $d_{AB}=4$, $d_{AD}=2$, $d_{AE}=8$, $d_{BD}=6$, $d_{BE}=7$, $d_{DE}=6$; diagonal zeros and symmetric entries complete the table.
Compare the three odd-vertex pairings: $(AB,DE)$, $(AD,BE)$ and $(AE,BD)$.
Their added costs are $10$, $9$ and $14$, so repeat $AD$ and $BE$.
The original edge total is $37+w=39$; any closed inspection route must correct all four odd degrees, requiring at least the least pairing cost.
A route attaining it is $A-B-E-F-A-D-C-B-E-D-A$.
The minimum is $39+9=48$ minutes.
For general $w$, $d_{AD}=\min(w,13)$, since the alternative shortest path is $A-B-C-D$.
The pairing $(AB,DE)$ always costs $4+6=10$.
The pairing $(AD,BE)$ costs $\min(w,13)+7$.
The third pairing costs $\min(w+6,11)+\min(w+4,9)$, which is $10+2w$ for $0<w\le5$ and $20$ for $w\ge5$.
The third pairing is never cheaper than $10$. The first two tie at $w=3$; repeat $AD,BE$ below $3$, or $AB,DE$ above $3$.
$L_c(w)=37+w+\min(w+7,10)=\begin{cases}44+2w,&0<w\le3,\\47+w,&w\ge3.\end{cases}$ Both formulas give $50$ at $w=3$.
After removing $AD$, only $B,E$ are odd and the remaining edge total is $37$.
Repeat shortest path $BE$ of length $7$, giving $37+7=44$ minutes.
The inspection obligation itself loses an edge, and the parity requirements change. A connection may shorten point-to-point travel while increasing the work required to inspect every link.
An open route from $A$ to $D$ requires exactly $A,D$ to remain odd.
Thus the extra traversals need only correct the odd degrees at $B,E$.
The shortest $B$ to $E$ path is the direct edge of length $7$ for every $w>0$.
$L_o(w)=37+w+7=44+w$. For example $A-B-E-F-A-D-C-B-E-D$ attains this total.
The open option including return costs $44+w+h$; its saving relative to the closed option is $\min(w,3)-h$.
Choose open strictly when $0<h<3$ and $w>h$. Choose closed strictly when $h>\min(w,3)$.
Tie when $h=\min(w,3)$: equivalently $w=h\le3$, or $h=3$ and $w\ge3$.

For $w\ge3$, the best closed route repeats $AB$ and $DE$ for $10$ minutes, while the open route repeats $BE$ for $7$. This fixed $3$-minute difference bounds the saving; increasing $w$ adds the same once-traversed link time to both routes.
